SPECIAL MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
SATURDAY - DECEMBER 2, 2023 - 10:00 A.M.
MALIBU ROOM - CERRITOS PARK EAST COMMUNITY CENTER
13234 E. 166TH STREET, CERRITOS, CA 90703
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at www.cerritos.us and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by phone at (562) 916-1248 during regular business hours.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting in person in the Malibu Room at the Cerritos Park East Community Center.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in person at the meeting or by using the following alternate methods:
Written correspondence (hard copy or email): Public comments can be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk no later than 12:00 p.m. on Friday, December 1, 2023. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 12:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting. During the meeting, your name and summary comments will be read into the record. The document will be retained with the public record of the meeting.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 916-1248 to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the meeting.

MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL HELD SATURDAY,
DECEMBER 2, 2023, 10:00 A.M., IN THE MALIBU ROOM AT THE CERRITOS PARK EAST
COMMUNITY CENTER, 13234 E. 166TH STREET, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA.

 1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 10:00 a.m.

 2.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Councilmember Lynda P. Johnson.

 3.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council were in attendance:

  Councilmember Lynda P. Johnson
  Councilmember Chuong Vo
  Councilmember Frank Aurelio Yokoyama
  Mayor Barrows Bruce W. Barrows

  MOTION: It was moved by Vo, and seconded by Yokoyama, to excuse Mayor Pro Tem
  Solanki from the meeting (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (4 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Johnson, Vo, Yokoyama, Barrows
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Solanki (excused)
  ABSTAIN:  None

 4.  New Business

 4A.  Review and consideration for the Cerritos City Council to establish the priority goals to
  guide the preparation of the City's Fiscal Year 2024-2025 Budget and Strategic Financial
  Plan in accordance with the Strategic Financial Plan and Budget Preparation Policy (Policy
  No. 2.04) (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Peter Kemp, Budget Manager. A PowerPoint presentation was
  displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  In-Person Public Comments:

  Matt Kauble inquired regarding the City’s plans for tree harvesting to offset the cost of tree
  reforestation, and the potential use of tree root barriers. He also suggested the City invest
  in an auto museum and institute an auto show to increase visitors to the City and tax
  revenue.

  Written Correspondence:
  (Written correspondence submitted by the deadline listed on the agenda is considered
  public record. Prior to the meeting, the Council received copies of the full-text unredacted
  written correspondence submitted for this item. Public requests for copies of the full-text
  redacted written correspondence can be made during regular business hours to the Office of
  the City Clerk/Treasurer.)

  Mike Ballentine submitted comments on various City-related items identified in the public
  agenda report.
 City of Cerritos  Saturday, December 2, 2023, 10:00 a.m.
City Council Special Meeting  Page 2 of 3

4.  New Business (continued)

4A.  (continued)

  Julie Xieu submitted comments on various City-related items identified in the public agenda
  report, Cerritos Center for the Performing Arts entertainment, the City calendar, and the
  Los Cerritos Center.

  Thomas Voth requested additional public notice time for Strategic Planning Sessions and
  submitted comments on various City-related items identified in the public agenda report.

  Gail Grossman requested enhanced accessibility at City facilities.

  Jay Miller requested improvements at freeway ramps in the City.

  Noting there were no other individuals who elected to provide public comment, the Mayor
  declared the public comments period closed.

  CONSENSUS (Barrows): Directed the City Manager to commence friendly talks with the
  California Department of Transportation (CalTrans) regarding the maintenance and
  landscaping of freeway ramps in Cerritos and provide an informational update to the City
  Council.

  CONSENSUS (Vo): Directed the City Manager to coordinate with the Los Angeles County
  Sheriff Department (LASD) to explore the potential use of drones for public safety in the
  City by LASD, and if necessary, with support of the California Contract Cities organization.
  If such program is not feasible with LASD, explore the options of developing a separate
  City-based public safety drone program.

  CONSENSUS (Vo): Directed the City Manager to coordinate with area agencies to examine
  the existing use of drones for public safety and conduct one or more site visits by February
  2024.

  CONSENSUS (Barrows): Directed the City Manager to research the feasibility of the City
  Manager and other key staff to attend AI-related training, similar to those conducted by
  Stanford and Harvard Universities, for the purpose of enhancing City-based government
  services. If attendance is feasible in FY 2023-24, the City Manager is authorized to process
  the appropriate budget amendment. If not feasible in FY 2023-24, include a proposal for
  such funding in the FY 2024-25 budget for City Council consideration.

  CONSENSUS (Barrows): Directed the City Manager to ensure the City has the full
  version of the OpenGov software platform and implements access to instructional tools (in
  various media formats) to facilitate effective use as soon as feasible.

  CONSENSUS (Barrows): Directed the City Manager to facilitate the selection of a
  professional firm to ensure best practices are utilized, including methods to encourage
  robust public participation, in the conduct of the City’s future strategic visioning and
  planning processes.

  CONSENSUS (Vo): Directed the City Manager to draft personalized letters from the City
  Council to Cerritos Sheriff Station deputies expressing support of their work in the City,
  with a copy available for public dissemination.

  CONSENSUS (Johnson): Directed the City Manager to schedule an agenda report for City
  Council review and consideration of a resolution in support of the Cerritos Sheriff Station
  deputies.
 City of Cerritos  Saturday, December 2, 2023, 10:00 a.m.
City Council Special Meeting  Page 3 of 3

4.  New Business (continued)

4A.  (continued)

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Johnson, to direct the City Manager
  to:

  1. Compile the input and information received at this meeting as related to development
  of Fiscal Year 2024-25 priority goals, including removal of the proposed “coyote issues”
  item as the City Council has previously provided consensus direction on the matter;
  and

  2. Work in collaboration with the City Council Budget and Finance Ad Hoc Working Group
  to review the compiled input and information and develop proposed measurable
  objectives and tasks; and

  3. Schedule an agenda report at an upcoming meeting for City Council review and
  consideration of approval of final priority goals, objectives, and tasks for use in guiding
  the preparation of the Fiscal Year 2024-25 Citywide Budget.

  The motion carried (4 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Johnson, Vo, Yokoyama, Barrows
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Solanki (excused)
  ABSTAIN:  None

5.  Adjournment

  The meeting adjourned at 1:32 p.m.

  _/s/ Cynthia Nava__________
  Cynthia Nava
  Assistant City Clerk
